verdict.line: You lose if you let Darius close to Apprehend (E) range and stack Hemorrhage to five before you can disengage; you win if you poke with Q and E from outside 535 range and force the fight onto your tentacles instead of his stacks.

brief.thesis: Illaoi's Q (850 range) and E (900 range) both outreach Darius's entire threat radius — his E (Apprehend) only pulls from 535, and his Q (Decimate) is a stationary swing, not a dash. The whole lane is a fight over that gap: whoever controls whether Darius gets to melee range decides the trade, since once he's there his Hemorrhage stacks and enrage bonus AD turn every extended fight in his favor. The 49.8% win rate over 1018 games reflects that this is genuinely a coinflip decided by who plays the range correctly, not a hard-favored matchup either way.

theirWindow.what: Darius can hook you from 535 range and immediately follow with Q (Decimate) and W (Crippling Strike) to stack Hemorrhage fast. Pre-level 6 this kills you outright if you don't have Flash up, per the measured matchup data — his E cooldown starts at 26s and drops to 16s by rank 5, so track it and don't stand at 535-650 range when it's about to come off cooldown.

yourWindow.when: when Darius's E (Apprehend) is on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Poke freely with Q (850 range, 10/9/8/7/6s cooldown) and E (900 range, 16/15/14/13/12s cooldown) since neither is inside his effective reach without the hook. Test of Spirit forces him to either eat the echoed damage standing still or walk toward you to break it, and either choice loses him tempo you can convert into Vessel pressure.

start.why: Highest measured win rate (52.5% over 739 games) — the extra sustain and AD matter because you're winning this lane on poke trades, not all-ins.

boots.why: 51.7% win rate over 877 games; Darius's damage is entirely physical autos and Q/W procs, so the flat reduction blunts his stack-and-burst combo directly.

core.why: Highest-winning core path (64.1% over 117 games) as first item; the armor shred lets your tentacle and Q damage keep scaling as he stacks armor to survive your poke.
Second in the same 64.1% path; the slow on proc helps you disengage before he closes to Apprehend range, which is the single biggest thing that kills you in this matchup.
Third in the top build path; the HP and tenacity-adjacent survivability matters directly against his true-damage R once he's stacked Hemorrhage.

situational.when: he's ahead and bleeding you down over extended trades
he's snowballed and his enrage-boosted autos are outhealing your tentacle sustain
you want an earlier lifesteal-adjacent spike to win the all-in at 6

runes.keystoneWhy: Highest-winning page (53.3%, 36.9% pick); the free HP and proc damage reward you for the long, drawn-out poke trades this matchup is decided by, and the extra health buys you the margin to survive getting hooked once before 6.

summoners.why: This combo has the highest measured win rate (55.2%, 16.5% pick). Flash is close to mandatory pre-6 — the matchup data explicitly warns you die to Apprehend without it — and Ignite lets you convert the E poke advantage into a kill instead of letting his Q healing undo your damage. Exhaust+Flash (53%, 31.2% pick) is the safer alternative if you'd rather blunt his all-in outright once he lands the hook.

playing.title: Poke with E, not W
playing.detail: Test of Spirit (900 range) lets you damage him without entering his 535 Apprehend range or his melee Q swing. Harsh Lesson (400 range leap) puts you in both, so save it for after he's already committed.

playing.title: Track his E cooldown windows
playing.detail: Apprehend runs 26/23.5/21/18.5/16s. Trade aggressively with Q autos and even W leaps the moment it's down; back off and only poke with Q/E as it approaches coming back up.

playing.title: Disengage before three stacks
playing.detail: Hemorrhage stacks to five and enrages him with a large AD bonus at max stacks. Break off the trade once you see three stacks rather than fighting through to see if you win the exchange.

playing.title: Hold Flash for the hook, not the kill
playing.detail: Pre-6 you most likely die if pulled by Apprehend without Flash, per the measured matchup note. Don't burn it to chase — burn it to survive the pull.

playing.title: All-in only after level 6
playing.detail: Leap of Faith spawns a tentacle on every enemy hit, so land it into a follow-up Harsh Lesson so the tentacles focus him too. Before 6 your all-in win rate is weak; don't force it.

playing.title: Punish a whiffed Decimate
playing.detail: Decimate is a wind-up swing in place, not a dash — if he misses it he's briefly committed and out of position for a W leap trade.

playing.title: Respect true damage at high stacks
playing.detail: Noxian Guillotine deals true damage that scales with his Hemorrhage stacks and refreshes its cooldown on a kill. Don't sit at execute range once he's above three stacks on you.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, summoners, and win rates above are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning, timing windows, and trade patterns are our own tactical read applied on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: A pre-level 6 Illaoi will most likely be killed if she is pulled by Darius’s (E) if you do not use Flash. Try to stay outside the range of (E) and farm with your [Q]. Even after you strike him with [E], fall back if Darius closes in to use (E). If you must engage in close quarters, be careful not to stay in range of his (Q).
